standard_prerequisites.name: Karoubian categories
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the two equivalent descriptions of a Karoubian category, in particular the dual description invoked for the second assertion of the proof.

standard_prerequisites.name: Kernels as representing objects
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the definition of a kernel and its description by a representable functor
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the observation that the functor sending an object W to the kernel of the induced endomorphism of the Hom-set is representable exactly when the idempotent has a kernel.

core_obligations: Setup (proof lines 772-777): for an idempotent e : X -> X the functor sending W to the kernel of the endomorphism of Hom(W, X) induced by e is representable exactly when e admits a kernel.

Kernels of idempotents of abelian groups (proof lines 778-792): for an idempotent endomorphism e of an abelian group the kernel of e is equal to the kernel of the endomorphism of the countable product displayed in the proof and defined componentwise.

The right inverse (proof lines 793-801): the displayed map has an explicit right inverse, so the kernel in question exists by the hypothesis on the category; hence the first assertion holds, and the second is dual, using the dual description of a Karoubian category.
proof_roadmap: Translate the existence of kernels of idempotents into representability of an associated functor.
Express the kernel of an idempotent endomorphism of an abelian group as the kernel of a map on a countable product.
Provide a right inverse of that map and invoke the hypothesis on the category.
difficulty_reason: The lemma gives conditions under which a preadditive category is Karoubian: the existence of countable products together with kernels of maps having a right inverse, or dually countable coproducts together with cokernels of maps having a left inverse (statement lines 761-770). The proof is a complete argument: the existence of kernels of idempotents is recast as representability of an associated functor (proof lines 772-777); the kernel of an idempotent endomorphism of an abelian group is written as the kernel of a map on a countable product (proof lines 778-792); and that map is exhibited with a right inverse, so the hypothesis of the first assertion applies, the second following by duality (proof lines 793-801). The non-formal content is the countable product trick. The claim is H2: a structured argument with each input named.
